summary: A four-legged village animal - barrel body, arched neck, horned head, three-segment legs and a tail - with a procedural diagonal-pair walk cycle, route following and a clamped turn rate.
objective: Seen from about three metres the animal reads as three tiers of detail: body, neck and tail silhouette, then jointed legs, muzzle, ears and horns, then hoof splits, eye highlights and nostrils; in motion the diagonal legs pair up and the planted hoof does not slide.
intent_signals: add a walking animal to the village
example_prompts: Put a goat on the lane and have it walk between the well and the barn.
I need a four-legged animal whose legs actually plant on the ground.
not_for: Anatomically accurate animal locomotion or veterinary reference.
Any claim about the gait of a named species.
Skinned or blend-shape deformation: this rig is rigid parts on rotating joints.

silhouette: barrel trunk tapering from a 0.43 m chest to a 0.34 m rump, back line 0.88 m above the ground
neck leaning forward 24 degrees into a horned head that breaks the back line at 1.18 m
tail carried up and away from the rump, and four legs whose gaps are readable between them
in motion: the diagonal pairs split the silhouette, one pair grounded while the other swings
medium: three-segment legs - thigh, shin and fetlock - with the foreleg elbow folding back and the hind stifle folding forward
muzzle, ears with a pale inner surface, and horns swept back off the skull
hooves that stay flat on the ground through stance and roll over the toe through swing
body bob of 2.2 cm at twice the stride rate, with the head nodding once per stride
fine: each hoof split into two claws about 3.6 cm across, chamfered at 1.2 cm
eyes 4.8 cm across with a 1.4 cm highlight, and 2.2 cm nostril dots on the muzzle
three growth rings turned into each horn
per-seed jitter on ear splay and hoof claw offset, so two animals are not one animal twice

principles: Fix the body plan first - four legs, one neck, one tail - then let the gait follow from it; a creature that changes limb count between poses stops reading as an organism.
Drive the feet from the distance travelled, never from wall-clock time: phase advances by travel divided by stride length, so the same walk holds together at any speed.
The stance foot is the contact with the world. Author its ground span to equal the body travel of that stance and the sliding-puppet look disappears without any IK solver at runtime.
implementation: Call create({ scale, strideM, strideHz, speed, seed, coat, yawRateRad }); the group is centred on its footprint with y = 0 at the ground plane and the animal facing +Z.
Call animate(dt) every frame; it returns false for dt <= 0 and true when the pose advanced. animate(dt, speed) overrides the cruise speed for that frame onward.
speed = 0 means cruise, which is strideM x strideHz x scale; set it explicitly to walk faster or slower than the authored gait.
setRoute(points, loop) takes [x, z] or [x, y, z] points, drops the walker on the first point and turns it towards each next one at no more than yawRateRad; a non-looping route ends in a halt.
Read state.position, state.heading, state.phase and state.distance for a follow camera or a footstep sound; do not write them while a route is running.
Sockets are ordered harness, head, back: the proof harness aims its detail view at sockets[0] and lifts that anchor by 0.35 of the model height, so the chest socket is what frames the head.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
Step animate(1/60) for four seconds and log the world position of hoof-0: through each stance run its x and z must vary by less than 2 cm (kits-creatures.test.js asserts this).
hoof-0 and hoof-3 must share a height at every frame, and differ from hoof-1 and hoof-2: that is the diagonal pairing, visible as a trot-like walk.
The same seed and the same dt sequence must reproduce the same pose exactly.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry and an authored gait. Nothing here is a measurement of any real animal, and no biomechanical claim is made.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters.
The foot plant is exact only while the walker travels in a straight line; a turn moves the planted foot along the arc, by up to the turn radius times the yaw step.
Rigid parts on rotating joints, no skinning: joints show as hard creases at close range, which is why the fetlock and shoulder masses are separate spheres.

far.png, mid.png, close.png and detail.png are single frames of the delivered mid-stride pose; close-motion.png is the same view after kit-proof.py --motion-check advances animate(dt) by a fixed number of 1/60 s steps, so the walk cycle is proved by two frames, not by a film.
create() returns the rig posed mid-stride rather than in its rest pose, so a single still reads as walking; the socket positions are still read off the rest pose, so they do not move with phase.

T2 is the same geometry with runtime procedural surface and vertex occlusion (see knowledge.surface-tier-defaults); it adds no polygons and ships no files, and it reads at stylized-game quality, not photoreal.
creative_affordances: Push scale to 0.5 for a dog or to 2.0 for an ox; the gait keeps working because every length in the cycle is derived from strideM.
Swap coat and re-seed for a herd that reads as one species with different individuals.
Drop the horns and shorten the neck for a farm dog; the leg chain does not care.

defaults.rationale: A 0.62 m stride at 1.1 Hz is 0.68 m/s, a walk a 1.7 m figure keeps up with; the 0.62 duty factor keeps two feet grounded for most of the cycle, which is what separates a walk from a trot at this speed.

T0.note: Bevelled box from the proof log bounds; the standing pose, not the stride envelope.

T2.note: Proved at the fur family added in phase 10C. The pelt colours #b39a78 (coat) and #ded0b6 (belly) map to fur; horn #e2d3ae, hoof #332c26, nose #6b504a, eye #1d1916 and the eye spark #fff6e2 have no family and stay flat on purpose, so about 47 percent of the triangles are unmapped -- keratin, horn and wet skin are not fur. Fabric, tried in phase 9D, failed here because a 24-thread weave is a *pattern* at 8 cm and read as basketwork; fur is a millimetre-scale directional strand field with no structure at any scale, so the magnification kit-surface applies to a 0.08-0.21 m limb (repeat 0.32 to 0.84 against the 0.25 m pitch) only coarsens it. Judged on the frames: at the 2.15 m close view the coat reads as short hair with low-frequency tone patches and contact shading at the joints; at the 0.75 m detail view the extruded head and neck plates, which take metre UVs and so the finest repeat, read as a regular ribbing rather than as hair.

T3.note: No baked glTF ships for this blueprint: phase 9C baked only the two heroes (timber-cottage and watermill).

T4.note: No external asset ships with this skill.
